item.text: The workspace is essentially a blank Node project, so I’m setting up a small native Node server with a JSON-backed API and a responsive browser UI. Book detail pages will have stable `/book/<id>` URLs so they can be shared directly.

The core flows are in place: the shelf separates reading and finished books, the form captures title, author, and notes, and each book opens at a shareable URL. I’m adding a short run guide and reviewing the assembled files for any obvious integration issues.

One edge case surfaced in review: two saves arriving together could each write from the same old JSON snapshot, causing one book to be lost. I’m tightening the file update path so each create or status change reads and writes in sequence.

Built Leaf, a small reading tracker with an “in progress” shelf, a finished shelf, a form for titles, authors, and notes, and controls to change a book’s status. Each book has a detail page at `/book/<id>` with a share button. Books persist in [data/books.json](/workspace/data/books.json).

Start it with `npm start`, then open http://localhost:3000. To open a shared link, the person receiving it needs to be able to reach the machine running the app.

I didn’t run a test suite.
